biggest_gap.what: Every person in Black Marsh now stands their own way and breathes on their own phase, and I have photographed it and located it in pixels. **There are still FOURTEEN distinct rendered bodies serving 408 NPC records — one per 29.14, against a bar of one per 12.** Re-derived this turn on the r9 critic's own instrument: the reachable pool is 9 bodies for `saxhleel` and 5 for `humanoid`; the `actor` arm is 32 for 408 (one per 12.75, needing 34) with `townsman` alone at 97 = 23.8% against a 10% ceiling; and 93 pairs of identically-rendered NPCs stand within 15 m of each other in the same settlement (E4, unchanged for three verdicts). E3 finds three build bands of five — no child, no stooped-old, because `CHARACTER_SPECS` carries no age or spine-curvature axis at all. secondary_observations.note: **THE ROUND'S STRONGEST CLAIMED ARTEFACT RESTS ON AN ARM THAT IS ARITHMETICALLY INCAPABLE OF GOING RED, AND THE ROUND SAYS SO IN THE SENTENCE THAT OFFERS IT.** Its words: *'a required-to-disagree control of the frame compared with ITSELF at exactly 0 changed pixels of 2,073,600, which is what says the capture is deterministic and the changed pixels are the scene rather than the renderer.'* Read the instrument: `tools/visual/f10-r12-motion-pixels.mjs:104` is `CONTROL_frame_against_itself: diff(imgs[0].img, imgs[0].img, THRESH)` — the same decoded buffer passed twice. `diff` walks two buffers that are the same object; every delta is 0 by construction. It would read 0 on a corrupted decode, on a non-deterministic renderer, on a camera that moved. `out.CONTROL_ok` is a tautology and `out.pass` therefore reduces to `pairs.every(changed > 0)`. **It is also not a 'required-to-disagree' arm at all** — it is required to AGREE, and it agrees with itself. **SO I SHOT THE CONTROL THE CLAIM NEEDED.** `tools/visual/f10-r12c-motion-truth.mjs` captures `motion-t000.png`, then calls `stepFrames(0)` — valid, `engine.js:stepFrames` accepts 0 and still calls `loop.renderNow()` — and captures `motion-t000r.png`: the same simulation frame (both manifests record `sim_frame: 22`), the same camera by construction, two independent trips through the rasteriser, two independent PNG encodes. **Result: 0 changed pixels of 2,073,600, and the two files are byte-identical — md5 a5c6c8733482e2d859af45cb2a5cf140 for both.** The capture IS deterministic. **The round's conclusion is right and its proof was not.** That distinction is the whole of CRITIC-DOCTRINE's method and it is why this is filed as HAZARDS §30 rather than shrugged at: a check that cannot fail is worth exactly nothing, however true the thing it asserts.

**A 2% FRAME CHANGE PROVES MOTION OF SOMETHING. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT A CROWD UNTIL IT IS LOCATED, AND NOBODY HAD LOCATED IT.** Lilmoth is a stilt town over water at 08:00, with foliage on the horizon; the round's own frames contain both. So my capture records, at every shot, each drawn NPC's screen-space box, projected from its BONE world matrices through the live camera matrices (HAZARDS §27 — read a bone, not the group). Then every changed pixel is asked where it landed. **My own consecutive series, one fixed camera at bearing 45, 24 sim frames apart:** t000->t024 **56,125 changed of 2,073,600 = 2.7066%, of which 83.65% fall inside NPC boxes covering 9.36% of the frame — an enrichment of 8.93x**; t024->t048 **32,682 = 1.5761%, 85.66% inside boxes covering 9.19% — 9.32x**; t048->t072 **32,031 = 1.5447%, 82.28% inside boxes covering 9.09% — 9.05x**. The residual 14-18% sits in a thin scatter near the horizon and in the shadow under the moving figures, which is what you would expect and which nobody should score. **THIS IS THE STATEMENT THE ROUND WANTED AND COULD NOT MAKE**: the breathing does not merely change the frame, it changes the frame ON THE PEOPLE, at nine times the rate area alone would predict. Independently, my series replicates the SHAPE of the round's — a large first step then two smaller ones — on a different session at a different phase, which is the right kind of agreement between two runs that were never going to produce the same integers.

**JOB 2, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST THING IN THE ROUND. VERIFIED BY FALSIFICATION, NOT BY READING.** HAZARDS §28's claim is that arm 9 replays the real clock jump (24 -> 84) and is required to FAIL the design the round started with. I built two control clones per §22 — `git archive HEAD game tools` into a scratch tree, no `.git`, each running THE CLONE'S OWN copy of the tool against the clone's own `game/` — and patched only `poseStatic`'s re-solve condition. **Arm 9 on the shipped WINDOW form: starved 0 of 120. On the MODULO form `t % N === bucket`: starved 106 of 120. On a tree with the re-solve branch deleted entirely: starved 120 of 120.** So the arm discriminates three designs and not two, and 106/120 = 11.7% survival matches both the 1-of-8-buckets expectation and the round's own live 7.41%. **AND IT IS THE ONLY ARM OF THE FIFTEEN THAT CATCHES IT**: in the modulo clone, 13 of 15 arms stay green (the fourteenth is arm 2, which fails only because `git archive HEAD game tools` does not carry the corpus artifact it re-derives). That is §28's rule proved on its own example. The round wrote the arm that fails its own shipped design, banked the failing run rather than deleting it, and filed the hazard. It is the single best piece of method in twelve rounds of F10 and it should be said plainly.

**THE ROUND LABELLED THIS AN INFERENCE AND ASKED A CRITIC TO CONVERT IT. I RAN `--stages=stability` AND IT CONVERTS.** Its S59 clause-(b) arms report bones bit-identical at a pinned clock on 31 of 60 across REBUILD, TRAVEL and SAVE/RELOAD, and it argued — explicitly labelling it an inference — that 31 is the DRAWN population because an invisible actor is never advanced and therefore holds whatever clock it was born at. **JOB 5. A BUILDER REWRITING A PRESERVATION CLAUSE IT CANNOT MEET IS EXACTLY WHAT S59 EXISTS TO POLICE, SO I CHECKED THE REASONING RATHER THAN THE CONCLUSION. THE RULING HOLDS AND THE SUBSTITUTE IS STRONGER, NOT WEAKER.** Clause (b) as the r11 critic wrote it asks that the stance probe's REBUILD / TRAVEL / SAVE-RELOAD arms 'still return 60 of 60 bit-identical' bone signatures, and that probe reads bones at two wall times with frames in between. Arm (b2), filed in the SAME verdict, requires the bones to differ 60 frames apart. Both cannot hold: literal compliance with (b) is achievable only by not doing the round. **The test of whether the split is honest or convenient is the clause's own stated reason, and the r11 critic wrote it down**: *'a crowd that re-rolls on stream-in is a worse defect than a crowd that is still'*. That is a statement about being dealt a new HAND — weight-bearing side, depth, phase offset, rate, head aim, torso twist, stoop, arm and elbow and splay draws — not about being at the same point in a breath. The split the round makes is exactly along that line: identity invariant, phase a function of (identity, sim frame), measured both ways at a pinned clock. **It is strictly stronger than the clause as written on the property the clause exists to protect**, because a bit-identical bone signature could in principle be produced by two different hands landing on the same pose, whereas comparing the seeded record directly cannot. And the pin costs nothing it does not declare: the round declares the `sim.frame` write as a method deviation rather than leaving it to be found, and 8 frames is one full stagger window, which is the smallest pin under which every bucket has fired once in both arms. **The strongest of the three arms is SAVE/RELOAD, and for a reason the round states and I confirmed in the source it cites: `loadState()` resets `sim.frame` to 0, so the clock is destroyed and rebuilt and every person still comes back with the same dealt hand — 60 of 60.** RULING: the substitute clause is adopted, it is as strong as (b) on (b)'s own stated purpose and stronger on the mechanism, and I have carried it into my own gap's preservation clause (b) above in the split form.
